KNOWN BUG: When a child of the dialog uses autoFocus, focus does not return to the element that opened the dialog after it closes. Rules: - Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure. === REVIEW 1 FINDINGS === - [blocking] Dialog: after a backdrop click with the parent ignoring onOpenChange, focus is on BODY, outside the dialog. Tab then moves to the page's opener button, and Escape does nothing because the keydown never reaches the dialog's handler. Probe D1/D2/D20 (`user.click(document.querySelector("[data-backdrop]"))`, then `user.tab()`). Observed: `active=BODY`, and after Tab `active=`. Expected: focus stays inside the dialog, and Escape calls `onOpenChange(false)`. The cause is that the backdrop is a non-focusable div, and the trap and Escape only listen on the dialog element. - [blocking] Combobox: an active option that becomes disabled while open can still be chosen with Enter. Probe C1c: options `[apple, fig]`, ArrowDown (apple active), rerender with apple `disabled: true`, then Enter. Observed: `onChange.mock.calls` = `[["apple"]]`. Expected: no call. The cause is that `handleKeyDown` for Enter checks only `activeOption`, not `disabled`. - [minor] Dialog with `description={0}` renders a bare "0" text node outside any `

` and sets no `aria-describedby` (`{description &&

The spec doesn't require click-to-open, so this is a UX note only. - [minor] Combobox: `aria-expanded` is true while "No results" is showing, but there is no listbox, so `aria-controls` points to nothing. This is a variant of the already-known aria-controls issue. - [minor] Tabs: uncontrolled selection with no `defaultValue` is derived as `enabledValues[0]`, not stored.
